Basis of Presentation
The accompanying unaudited consolidated financial statements have been prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) in the United States for interim financial reporting and pursuant to the rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). These financial statements reflect all normal recurring adjustments that, in the opinion of management, are necessary for a fair presentation. The results of operations for the three months ended March 31, 2025 are not necessarily indicative of the results to be expected for the full year ending December 31, 2025.

Certain information and footnote disclosures normally included in annual financial statements prepared in accordance with GAAP have been condensed or omitted pursuant to SEC rules and regulations. These interim financial statements should be read in conjunction with the consolidated financial statements and notes thereto included in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024.

Principles of Consolidation
The consolidated financial statements include the accounts of Coterra Energy Inc. and its subsidiaries. All significant intercompany balances and transactions have been eliminated in consolidation. Investments in companies in which we do not have control, but have the ability to exercise significant influence, are accounted for using the equity method.

Use of Estimates
The preparation of financial statements in conformity with GAAP requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets, liabilities, revenues and expenses and disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities. Actual results could differ from those estimates.

Significant estimates include, but are not limited to, quantities of proved oil and gas reserves, future cash flows from oil and gas properties, fair value of derivative instruments, environmental obligations, asset retirement obligations, income taxes, fair value of assets acquired and liabilities assumed in business combinations, impairments of oil and gas properties and goodwill, and stock-based compensation. Management believes the estimates used in preparing the consolidated financial statements are reasonable and appropriate.

Recent Accounting Pronouncements
We monitor new accounting standards issued by the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) and other authoritative bodies for their potential impact on our financial statements. We have adopted all applicable standards that were effective during the periods presented. Standards issued but not yet adopted are currently being evaluated and are not expected to have a material impact on our financial position, results of operations or cash flows.

Note 5. Acquisitions and Divestitures
In December 2023, Coterra entered into an agreement to divest certain non-core oil and gas properties located in the Anadarko Basin. The divestiture closed in February 2024 and resulted in proceeds of approximately $215 million. The Company recognized a gain of $35 million on the sale, which is included in gain (loss) on asset sales in the Consolidated Statements of Operations for the three months ended March 31, 2024.

In March 2024, Coterra completed the acquisition of undeveloped acreage in the Delaware Basin for approximately $120 million in cash. The acquisition was accounted for as an asset acquisition and resulted in an increase to oil and gas properties on the Consolidated Balance Sheets. No goodwill was recorded in connection with the transaction.

Additionally, the Company periodically evaluates opportunities to monetize non-core assets to enhance financial flexibility and focus on its core operating areas. Proceeds from asset sales are expected to be used for general corporate purposes, including funding of the capital program, debt reduction and shareholder returns.

Dispositions subsequent to March 31, 2025, if any, will be disclosed in subsequent filings.

Note 7. Fair Value Measurements
The Company measures certain financial and non-financial assets and liabilities at fair value on a recurring or nonrecurring basis, depending on the nature of the instrument. Fair value is defined as the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. The Company utilizes market data or assumptions that market participants would use in pricing the asset or liability, including assumptions about risk and the risks inherent in the inputs to the valuation technique.

The Company prioritizes inputs to valuation techniques used to measure fair value into a three-level hierarchy:
- Level 1: Quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities.
- Level 2: Observable inputs other than quoted prices included within Level 1 that are observable for the asset or liability, either directly or indirectly.
- Level 3: Unobservable inputs that reflect the Company’s own assumptions about the assumptions market participants would use in pricing the asset or liability.

The following table presents the Company’s assets and liabilities measured at fair value on a recurring basis:

| (In millions) | Level 1 | Level 2 | Level 3 | Total |
|:--------------|--------:|--------:|--------:|------:|
| Derivative assets | 22 | 36 | — | 58 |
| Derivative liabilities | 14 | 29 | — | 43 |

The Company did not have any transfers between Levels 1, 2 and 3 during the periods presented. The fair value of derivative instruments is based on observable market data, including commodity prices, yield curves and credit spreads. The fair value of derivative instruments also incorporates credit risk adjustments to reflect the Company’s and counterparties’ nonperformance risk.

Nonrecurring fair value measurements primarily relate to the assessment of impairment of oil and gas properties and goodwill. The Company estimates the fair value of these assets using discounted cash flow techniques, which incorporate estimates of future commodity prices, production costs, development plans and discount rates. Significant judgment is involved in determining the assumptions used in the valuations, and changes in these assumptions could result in different fair value measurements and impairment charges.

Acquisitions and Divestitures
In November 2023, Devon completed the sale of certain non-core assets in the Williston Basin for proceeds of $410 million. A pre-tax gain of $75 million was recognized in connection with the sale and is included in “Other, net” in the Consolidated Statements of Earnings. The divested properties were classified as proved and unproved oil and gas properties within the Upstream segment. The sale does not represent a strategic shift that will have a major effect on Devon’s operations or financial results and, therefore, does not qualify as discontinued operations.

In January 2024, Devon entered into an agreement to acquire producing properties and undeveloped acreage in the Delaware Basin for approximately $2.1 billion, consisting of cash, stock consideration and the assumption of certain liabilities. The transaction closed in March 2024 and was accounted for as a business combination under ASC 805. The assets acquired include proved developed and undeveloped reserves, producing wells, drilling locations and related infrastructure. The preliminary purchase price allocation resulted in recognition of $1.7 billion of oil and gas properties, $250 million of goodwill and $150 million of asset retirement obligations. The purchase price allocation is preliminary and subject to change as additional information becomes available.

Devon continually evaluates its portfolio and may pursue additional acquisitions or divestitures to optimize its asset base and enhance shareholder value. The Company uses proceeds from divestitures to fund capital expenditures, reduce debt or return cash to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

Note 4. Business Combinations
On May 2, 2023, EOG completed the acquisition of Yates Petroleum Corporation and related entities for total consideration of approximately $2.5 billion, consisting of $1.8 billion in cash and $700 million in stock consideration. The transaction was accounted for as a business combination under ASC 805. The assets acquired included producing oil and gas properties, undeveloped acreage, gathering infrastructure and other related assets. The preliminary purchase price allocation resulted in the recognition of $2.2 billion of oil and gas properties, $200 million of goodwill and $100 million of asset retirement obligations.

The purchase price allocation is based on preliminary estimates and is subject to revision as additional information becomes available, including final valuations of assets acquired and liabilities assumed. The Company expects to finalize the purchase price allocation within 12 months of the acquisition date. Transaction costs of $25 million were incurred in connection with the acquisition and are included in general and administrative expenses in the Consolidated Statements of Income.

EOG continually evaluates acquisition opportunities to enhance its portfolio and expand its presence in core operating areas. The Company may fund future acquisitions through a combination of cash on hand, borrowings, equity issuances or other financing arrangements, depending on market conditions and the size and structure of the transaction.

Results of Operations
This section discusses certain year-to-year comparisons between 2024 and 2023, which should be read in conjunction with Item 7, Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations; the Consolidated Financial Statements and related Notes thereto, including the “Supplemental Information to Consolidated Financial Statements”; and the “Cautionary Statement Regarding Forward-Looking Information” included elsewhere in this report.

Overview

EOG’s operating performance in 2024 reflected the continued execution of its strategy to generate high returns on capital employed by focusing on premium drilling locations, controlling costs, and maintaining a strong balance sheet. Commodity prices experienced volatility during the year, influenced by global supply and demand dynamics, geopolitical events, and macroeconomic conditions. EOG’s disciplined capital allocation and operational efficiency allowed the company to deliver substantial free cash flow and significant returns to stockholders through dividends and share repurchases. The company continued to invest in high-return projects across its core U.S. plays, including the Delaware Basin and the Eagle Ford, while advancing its exploration program.

Net Operating Revenues

Net operating revenues decreased in 2024 compared to 2023, primarily due to lower realized commodity prices, partially offset by higher production volumes. The decrease in realized crude oil, natural gas, and NGL prices had a significant impact on revenues; however, increased production volumes and favorable differential improvements mitigated some of the decline. The company also benefited from improved marketing and transportation strategies that enhanced price realizations across regions.

Operating Expenses

Operating expenses increased modestly in 2024, driven by higher production taxes associated with increased production volumes and elevated cost inflation affecting materials and services. Lease and well expenses and transportation costs also rose year-over-year, reflecting activity levels and market conditions. EOG continued its focus on cost control initiatives, including supply chain optimization and operational efficiencies, to offset inflationary pressures.

Other Income (Expense)

Other income (expense) includes gains and losses on asset dispositions, interest income and expense, and other non-operating items. Interest expense decreased in 2024 due to lower average debt balances and favorable interest rates on outstanding borrowings.

Income Taxes

The effective tax rate for 2024 was influenced by changes in state tax rates and discrete items, including stock-based compensation and settlements of tax audits. EOG continues to evaluate tax planning strategies to optimize its overall tax position while ensuring compliance with applicable regulations.

Segment Reporting

EOG operates in a single segment, exploring for, developing, producing, and marketing crude oil, natural gas liquids, and natural gas. The company’s activities are managed on a consolidated basis for operational and financial reporting purposes.

Regional Results

United States

In the United States, EOG’s production volumes increased in 2024 across several core areas, particularly the Delaware Basin and the Eagle Ford, due to the company’s continued development drilling and completion activities. The company achieved improved well productivity through optimized completion designs, longer laterals, and enhanced reservoir characterization. Infrastructure investments supported production growth and reduced downtime associated with takeaway constraints.

Trinidad

Production in Trinidad was modestly lower in 2024 compared to 2023, reflecting natural declines and the timing of planned maintenance activities. EOG continues to evaluate opportunities to enhance production and extend field life through development projects and operational improvements.

Australia

EOG’s exploration activities offshore Australia continued in 2024, with seismic interpretation and prospect maturation advancing the company’s understanding of the region. The company is evaluating potential drilling opportunities subject to technical and commercial assessments.

Capital Expenditures

Capital expenditures in 2024 focused on high-return drilling programs, infrastructure projects to support production, and exploration for future growth. EOG maintained capital discipline, aligning investment levels with market conditions and expected returns.

Liquidity and Capital Resources

EOG maintained a strong financial position in 2024, supported by robust operating cash flows and prudent balance sheet management. The company had significant liquidity available through cash on hand and its unsecured revolving credit facility. EOG remains committed to returning capital to stockholders through dividends and share repurchases while investing in high-return opportunities.

Outlook

EOG’s strategy remains centered on generating sustainable long-term value by developing premium drilling opportunities, optimizing operations, and maintaining financial strength. The company will continue to monitor market conditions, adjust activity levels as appropriate, and pursue opportunities that align with its return objectives.

Term Loan

In December 2024, we entered into a $1.0 billion delayed draw term loan agreement (the “Term Loan”), which consisted of a single-draw term loan that was available for six months after entry into the agreement. In January 2025, in connection with the consummation of the Avant Merger, we borrowed the full $1.0 billion under the Term Loan. The Term Loan matures three years after funding. Borrowings under the Term Loan can be repaid in whole or in part without premium or penalty, and we are required to make repayments of principal under the Term Loan in quarterly installments, beginning with the last day of the Fiscal Quarter ending June 30, 2025, in an amount equal to (i) 1.25% of the aggregate principal amount of the Term Loan at any time outstanding during the Fiscal Quarters ending June 30, 2025 through March 31, 2026, (ii) 2.50% of the aggregate principal amount of the Term Loan at any time outstanding during the Fiscal Quarters ending June 30, 2026 through March 31, 2027 and (iii) 3.75% of the aggregate principal amount of the Term Loan at any time outstanding during the Fiscal Quarters ending June 30, 2027 through December 31, 2027. The remaining principal balance is due on the maturity date.

Borrowings under the Term Loan bear interest at a rate per annum equal to, at our option, either (i) a term SOFR plus a margin, or (ii) a base rate plus a margin. The applicable margin for term SOFR loans is 1.125% and the applicable margin for base rate loans is 0.125%. In addition, we are required to pay (a) a 0.10% per annum fee on any outstanding term SOFR loans, and (b) a ticking fee of 0.10% per annum on any unused portion of the Term Loan commitment during the availability period, in each case, payable quarterly in arrears.

The Term Loan contains customary affirmative and negative covenants, including, without limitation, financial, reporting and other covenants. The Term Loan contains a maximum leverage ratio covenant and a minimum interest coverage ratio covenant, in each case, as defined in the Term Loan. The Term Loan also contains customary events of default. The obligations under the Term Loan are guaranteed by certain of our existing and future domestic subsidiaries that guarantee our obligations under our Senior Notes and are unsecured.

The proceeds from the Term Loan were used to pay a portion of the cash consideration in the Avant Merger, to repay certain indebtedness of Avant, and to pay costs and expenses in connection with the Avant Merger. The remaining proceeds were used for general corporate purposes.

Revolving Credit Agreement

In November 2021, we entered into a $1.5 billion unsecured, senior revolving credit agreement (the “Revolving Credit Agreement”) with a scheduled maturity date of November 2026. In December 2024, we amended the Revolving Credit Agreement to (i) extend the scheduled maturity date to December 2029 and (ii) make certain other changes to the terms and conditions of the Revolving Credit Agreement. As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, there were no borrowings outstanding under the Revolving Credit Agreement and no letters of credit were issued. We were in compliance with all covenants under the Revolving Credit Agreement at December 31, 2024.

Borrowings under the Revolving Credit Agreement bear interest at a rate per annum equal to, at our option, either (i) a term SOFR plus a margin, or (ii) a base rate (which is equal to the highest of (a) the federal funds rate plus 0.50%, (b) the prime rate announced by JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., and (c) the term SOFR plus 1.00%) plus a margin. The applicable margin is based on our credit rating and ranges from 1.00% to 1.50% for term SOFR loans and from 0.00% to 0.50% for base rate loans. We also pay commitment fees on the average daily unused amount of the aggregate commitment ranging from 0.10% to 0.30% per annum, payable quarterly in arrears.

We have the right to increase the aggregate commitments under the Revolving Credit Agreement by up to an additional $750 million, subject to obtaining commitments from one or more financial institutions and certain other customary conditions. We also have the right to request the issuance of letters of credit under the Revolving Credit Agreement. The obligations under the Revolving Credit Agreement are guaranteed by certain of our existing and future domestic subsidiaries that guarantee our obligations under our Senior Notes and are unsecured.

We believe the Revolving Credit Agreement and the Term Loan provide us with financial flexibility and liquidity to meet our anticipated capital needs and to execute our business strategy. We intend to continue to maintain our investment grade credit profile and strong balance sheet.

Pricing. Crude oil, NGLs and natural gas prices have been volatile and often move independently. Changes in commodity prices contribute to varying operating results across EOG’s producing areas and may lead to changes in levels of drilling and completion activity. EOG utilizes a combination of firm transportation agreements, marketing arrangements and access to multiple markets to maximize netbacks and reduce exposure to regional price differentials. EOG continues to invest in technology, data analytics and automation to improve operational efficiency and performance.

EOG’s strategy prioritizes returns over growth, seeks to maintain a conservative balance sheet, and returns capital to shareholders through a sustainable dividend and, when appropriate, share repurchases. Contractual Obligations

The Company has various contractual obligations in the normal course of business, including obligations associated with gathering, processing and transportation agreements; drilling and completion services; equipment leases; and other service and supply contracts. These obligations are intended to support ongoing operations and development activities and may include both fixed and variable elements. The Company evaluates contractual obligations in the context of its operational plans, expected production levels and market conditions.

Gathering, Processing and Transportation Arrangements

The Company utilizes pipeline and processing infrastructure to move natural gas and NGLs from the wellhead to market. Agreements may include minimum volume commitments or capacity reservations, as well as fees for interruptible services, fuel and shrinkage. Commitments are structured to align with anticipated production and available infrastructure. The Company may incur deficiency payments if actual volumes do not meet contractual minimums. The Company monitors utilization of firm capacity and may adjust commitments through amendments, renegotiations or capacity releases to third parties when appropriate.

Market Access and Pricing

Realized prices for natural gas and NGLs are influenced by regional supply-demand dynamics, basis differentials and transportation availability. The Company’s marketing strategy includes contracting for transportation capacity to access premium markets and manage exposure to regional pricing differentials. The Company may use hedging instruments to mitigate commodity price risk and support cash flow stability. Hedging activities are evaluated based on market outlook, risk appetite and financial objectives.

Legal Matters

Securities Litigation

In October 2023, a putative securities class action lawsuit was filed in the United States District Court for the Southern District of Texas against the Company and certain of its current and former officers, alleging violations of federal securities laws. The complaint generally alleges that the defendants made false or misleading statements and failed to disclose certain information. The lawsuit seeks unspecified damages, interest, attorneys’ fees and other relief. The Company believes the claims are without merit and intends to defend itself vigorously. Additional lawsuits were also filed and have been consolidated with the Ezell lawsuit for pretrial proceedings. Because the outcome of litigation is inherently uncertain, the Company cannot predict the ultimate resolution or the range of potential loss, if any, associated with these matters.

Other Legal Proceedings

The Company is subject to various other legal and regulatory proceedings in the ordinary course of business, including matters related to environmental compliance, royalty and working interest owner disputes, personal injury and property damage claims and other contractual disputes. The Company evaluates legal proceedings on an ongoing basis and establishes accruals for loss contingencies when it is probable that a liability has been incurred and the amount of the loss can be reasonably estimated. The Company believes, based on current information and after consultation with counsel, that the ultimate resolution of these matters will not have a material adverse effect on its financial position, results of operations or cash flows. However, outcomes are inherently uncertain and estimates of potential losses could change as additional information becomes available.

Environmental Matters

The Company is subject to extensive federal, state and local environmental laws and regulations governing emissions to air, discharges to water, waste management and remediation of contaminated sites, among other matters. The Company endeavors to comply with applicable environmental requirements and to implement programs designed to minimize environmental impacts. The Company may incur capital expenditures and operating costs to maintain compliance with environmental regulations and to implement environmental initiatives. The ultimate cost of compliance may be affected by changes in laws or regulations, enforcement policies and other factors beyond the Company’s control.

Oil, Gas and NGL Marketing

The spot markets for oil, gas and NGLs are subject to volatility associated with changes in supply and demand fundamentals. Our results of operations and cash flows are highly dependent upon the prices we receive for oil, gas and NGLs and the quantities of those commodities that we produce. We generally sell our oil, gas and NGLs at pricing terms that reference a market index, with the price received influenced by issues associated with location and gathering and transportation arrangements. To promote the reliability of our sales revenues, we sell a portion of our production under both long-term and short-term contracts that may include fixed and variable pricing arrangements. We coordinate transportation and delivery logistics with buyers under these contracts and manage our exposure to regional and product-quality price differentials. We may also use basis swaps to influence these fractions in the overall sales price. A relatively small portion of our production is sold at variable, or market-sensitive, prices.

Additionally, we may enter into financial hedging arrangements to reduce our commodity price risk. Crude oil and condensate revenues in 2024 increased $173 million, or 2%, to $9,703 million from $9,530 million in 2023 due to an increase (decrease) in production ($426 million) and a lower composite average crude oil and condensate price ($253 million). The lower composite average crude oil and condensate price in 2024 compared to 2023 was due to a lower composite average realized price for U.S. production ($281 million), which was partially offset by a slightly higher composite average realized price for international and other production ($28 million). The effect of the lower composite average realized crude oil and condensate price in the U.S. compared to 2023 was partially offset by a higher U.S. composite average differential, excluding the effect of settled cash commodity derivative contracts. Although crude oil and condensate production in 2024 compared to 2023 decreased by 12.4 MMbbl (and 2024 compared to 2022 increased by 18.9 MMbbl), production increased primarily from the Permian Basin and was offset by lower production primarily in the Eagle Ford and Powder River Basin.

NGLs revenues in 2024 increased $222 million, or 12%, to $2,106 million from $1,884 million in 2023 due to an increase (decrease) in production ($168 million) and a higher composite average NGLs price ($54 million). The higher composite average NGLs price in 2024 compared to 2023 was due to a higher composite average realized price for U.S. production ($73 million), which was partially offset by a lower composite average realized price for international and other production ($19 million). NGLs production increased 10% to 165.0 MBbld (from 149.7 MBbld in 2023), primarily due to increased production in the Permian Basin and Utica and was partially offset by decreased production primarily in the Eagle Ford and Powder River Basin.

Natural gas revenues in 2024 decreased $193 million, or 11%, to $1,533 million from $1,726 million in 2023 due to an increase (decrease) in production ($80 million) and a lower composite average natural gas price ($273 million). The lower composite average natural gas price in 2024 compared to 2023 was due to a lower composite average realized price for U.S. production ($305 million), which was partially offset by a higher composite average realized price for international and other production ($32 million). Natural gas production increased 5% to 3,091 MMcfd (from 2,954 MMcfd in 2023). The increase in production was primarily due to increased production in the Permian Basin.

ITEMS 1 and 2. BUSINESS AND PROPERTIES
Coterra Energy Inc. (“Coterra,” the “Company,” “our,” “we” and “us”) is an independent oil and gas company engaged in the development, exploration and production of oil, natural gas and NGLs. Our assets are concentrated in areas with known hydrocarbon resources, which are conducive to multi-well, repeatable development programs. We operate in one segment, oil and natural gas development, exploration and production, in the continental U.S.

Our headquarters is located in Houston, Texas. We also maintain regional offices in Midland, Texas, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and Tulsa, Oklahoma, as well as field offices near our operations.

 STRATEGY
Coterra is a premier U.S.-focused exploration and production company. We embrace innovation, technology and data, as we work to create value for our investors and the communities where we operate. We believe the following strategic priorities will help drive value creation and long-term success.

Generate Sustainable Returns. Our premier assets across multiple basins provide commodity diversification and defensive positioning through the commodity price cycles that, combined with our disciplined capital investment, give us confidence in our ability to provide returns to our stockholders that we believe to be sustainable. Over the past three years, we have increased our annual base dividend $0.24 per share, or 40 percent, on our common stock to $0.84 per share and have returned over $3.5 billion to stockholders through dividends. Demonstrating our continued confidence in our business model, in February 2025, our Board of Directors increased our annual base dividend to $0.88 per share. During 2024, we also repurchased 17 million shares of our common stock for $464 million, at a weighted average share price of $26.35 per share under our current $2.0 billion share repurchase program, and have $1.1 billion available for future repurchases. We remain committed to returning 50 percent or more of our annual free cash flow to our stockholders through dividends and our share repurchase program, while maintaining our top-tier balance sheet.

Disciplined Capital Allocation Across Top-Tier Position. Our asset portfolio offers scale, duration, commodity optionality and resilient investment returns. We anticipate our drilling inventory will be developed over the next 20 to 30 years. With operations in the Permian Basin, Marcellus Shale and Anadarko Basin, our asset portfolio is both commodity and geographically diversified, allowing for capital allocation flexibility that may prove opportunistic in navigating commodity price cycles. During 2024 and 2023, we invested 63 percent and 57 percent, respectively, of our cash flow from operations in our capital programs, and in 2025 we expect to invest approximately 50 percent of our cash flow from operations, based on recent strip prices, including future expenses related to our recently completed acquisitions. We are committed to maintaining a disciplined capital investment strategy to maximize capital efficiency and create value for stockholders.

Maintain Financial Strength. Maintaining a top-tier balance sheet with significant financial flexibility is imperative in a cyclical industry exposed to commodity price volatility. Our asset base, revenue diversity, low-cost structure and strong balance sheet provide us with the flexibility to thrive across various commodity price environments. At year-end 2024, we had a $2.0 billion cash balance, $2.0 billion of unused commitments under our revolving credit agreement and a $1.0 billion undrawn term loan, successfully positioning us to fund the FME and Avant acquisitions that closed in January 2025 while maintaining our balance sheet strength. In January 2025, we borrowed $1.0 billion under the term loan to partially fund the closing of the FME and Avant acquisitions. For additional information refer to “Acquisitions” below, “Liquidity and Capital Resources” in Item 7, and Note 2 and Note 4 of the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements “Acquisitions” and “Long-Term Debt and Credit Agreements”.

Focus on Safe, Responsible and Sustainable Operations. The safety of our employees and contractors is the cornerstone of our focus on operational excellence. We empower all employees and contractors to utilize our Stop Work Authority program, which allows them to stop any work at any time if they are uncomfortable, discover a dangerous condition, or suspect any other EHS hazard. We are also focused on making our operations more environmentally sustainable by actively implementing technology across our operations from the design phase to equipment improvements to limit our methane emissions and flaring activity. We focus on practical and sustainable environmental initiatives that promote efficient use of fresh and produced water, eliminate or mitigate releases, and minimize land surface impact. We are committed to being responsible stewards of our resources and implementing sustainable practices. We have published our 2024 Sustainability Report, which includes more information related to our sustainability practices, on our website at www.coterra.com. The information on our website is not part of, and is not incorporated into, this Annual Report on Form 10-K or any other report we may file with or furnish to the SEC (and is not deemed filed herewith), whether before or after the date of this Annual Report on Form 10-K and irrespective of any general incorporation language therein.

6

 2024 OUTLOOK
Our 2024 capital program is expected to be in the range of $2.0 billion to $2.3 billion. We expect to drill approximately 140 to 150 net wells and turn in line approximately 145 to 155 net wells in 2024 across our three core operating areas. Our exploration and production capital will be focused on developing our high-return opportunities in all three operating areas, including liquids-rich opportunities in the Delaware and Midland basins of the Permian Basin as well as dry gas development in the Marcellus Shale. Our capital allocation is expected to be flexible and returns focused, and we may adjust activity across assets in response to commodity prices and other market conditions.

We plan to run an average of approximately 11 drilling rigs and three completion crews in 2024, with about seven drilling rigs and one and a half completion crews in the Permian Basin, two drilling rigs and one completion crew in the Marcellus Shale and two drilling rigs and one half of a completion crew in the Anadarko Basin. We will continue to deploy technologies, including e-frac fleets and automated drilling systems, and to optimize well designs to improve capital efficiency and reduce cycle times. We expect infrastructure investment to include gathering systems, compression, water handling and disposal and other field infrastructure.

Our production mix in 2024 is expected to be approximately 30% oil, 58% natural gas and 12% NGLs. We anticipate that production volumes will be relatively flat compared to 2023 on a Boe basis, with modest oil growth. We expect differentials to benchmark pricing to be consistent with recent periods, subject to market conditions, seasonal factors and ongoing midstream constraints. We intend to maintain a robust hedging program to mitigate volatility in cash flows and to protect returns across our capital program while preserving upside exposure.

We will continue to evaluate our capital allocation across our three core operating areas and make adjustments as appropriate based on commodity prices, well performance, service costs, supply chain dynamics and other factors. We remain focused on maximizing free cash flow, maintaining balance sheet strength and returning capital to shareholders through our base dividend, variable dividends and share repurchases as appropriate.

We expect to fund our 2024 capital program with cash on hand and cash flow from operations, supplemented by our revolving credit facility as needed for working capital timing. We believe our liquidity and financial position provide flexibility to execute our program and to pursue bolt-on acquisitions and other value-enhancing opportunities as they arise.

We will continue to monitor and manage environmental, health and safety risks associated with our operations. Our sustainability initiatives include reducing greenhouse gas emissions intensity, reducing methane emissions, flaring and venting, and improving water recycling and reuse. We also plan to continue investing in community engagement and workforce development programs in the areas where we operate.

Crude oil and condensate revenues in 2024 increased $173 million, or 1%, to $13,921 million from $13,748 million in 2023, primarily due to an increase in production ($491 million), partially offset by a lower composite average crude oil and condensate price ($318 million). EOG's composite crude oil and condensate price for 2024 decreased 2% to $77.40 per barrel compared to $79.17 per barrel in 2023. Crude oil and condensate production in 2024 increased 3% to 491 MBbld as compared to 476 MBbld in 2023. The increased production was primarily in the Permian Basin and Utica.

NGLs revenues in 2024 increased $222 million, or 12%, to $2,106 million from $1,884 million in 2023 primarily due to an increase in production ($192 million) and a higher composite average NGLs price ($30 million). EOG's composite average NGLs price increased 1% to $23.40 per barrel in 2024 compared to $23.07 per barrel in 2023. NGLs production in 2024 increased 10% to 246 MBbld as compared to 224 MBbld in 2023. The increased production was primarily in the Permian Basin.

Natural gas revenues in 2024 decreased $193 million, or 11%, to $1,551 million from $1,744 million in 2023 primarily due to a lower composite natural gas price ($435 million), partially offset by an increase in natural gas deliveries ($242 million). EOG's composite average natural gas price decreased 22% to $2.17 per Mcf in 2024 compared to $2.79 per Mcf in 2023. Natural gas deliveries in 2024 increased 14% to 1,948 MMcfd as compared to 1,711 MMcfd in 2023. The increase in production was primarily due to increased production of associated natural gas from the Permian Basin and higher natural gas deliveries in Trinidad.

During 2024, EOG recognized net gains on the mark-to-market of financial commodity and other derivative contracts of $204 million, which included net cash received from settlements of natural gas financial commodity derivative contracts of $214 million. The net gains of $204 million included gains of $110 million related to the Brent crude oil (Brent) linked gas sales contract. During 2023, EOG recognized net gains on the mark-to-market of financial commodity and other derivative contracts of $818 million, which included net cash paid for settlements of crude oil, NGLs and natural gas financial commodity derivative contracts of $112 million.

Gathering, processing and marketing revenues are revenues generated from sales of third-party crude oil, NGLs and natural gas, as well as fees associated with gathering third-party natural gas and revenues from sales of EOG-owned sand. Purchases and sales of third-party crude oil and natural gas may be utilized in order to balance firm capacity at third-party facilities with production in certain areas and to utilize excess capacity at EOG-owned facilities. EOG sells sand primarily in order to balance the timing of firm purchase agreements with completion operations. Marketing costs represent the costs to purchase third-party crude oil, natural gas and sand and the associated transportation costs, as well as costs associated with EOG-owned sand sold to third parties.

Gathering, processing and marketing revenues less marketing costs in 2024 decreased $14 million compared to 2023, primarily due to lower margins on sand sales and natural gas marketing activities, partially offset by higher margins on crude oil marketing activities.

Proved Undeveloped Reserves
At December 31, 2023, the Company had PUD reserves of 482 MMBoe, a decrease of 100 MMBoe compared to 582 MMBoe as of December 31, 2022. The decrease in 2023 was primarily due to transfers of 265 MMBoe of PUD reserves to proved developed, partially offset by 190 MMBoe of additions from the Company’s development and appraisal programs, 19 MMBoe of positive revisions to previous estimates and 18 MMBoe of acquisitions.

In 2023, the Company commenced development on 16 MMBoe of PUD reserves. As of December 31, 2023, the Company had 482 MMBoe of PUD reserves with approximately 59 percent in the Marcellus Shale, 33 percent in the Permian Basin and 8 percent in the Anadarko Basin. We anticipate we will develop approximately 54 percent, 78 percent and 85 percent of these PUD reserves by 2026, 2027 and 2028, respectively. As of December 31, 2023, all PUD reserves are scheduled to be developed within five years from the date of initial booking in accordance with the SEC five-year rule. The Company had no PUD reserves that had remained undeveloped for five years or more since initial disclosure of those reserves. Future development plans for our PUD reserves include drilling or participating in approximately 34 gross (28.7 net) wells in the Permian Basin, 37 gross (31.4 net) wells in the Marcellus Shale and six gross (5.3 net) wells in the Anadarko Basin, with associated facilities and infrastructure.

The following table provides a reconciliation of the change in the Company’s PUD reserves (MMBoe):

PUD reserves increased by 211 MMBoe in 2022 compared to 2021. In addition to the effect of sales and purchases of reserves in place, the increase was primarily due to 264 MMBoe of additions from the Company’s development and appraisal programs and 34 MMBoe of positive revisions to previous estimates, partially offset by 73 MMBoe of transfers of PUD reserves to proved developed. In 2022, the Company commenced development on 13 MMBoe of PUD reserves.

The Company believes that it has the capacity to fund the development of its PUD reserves through a combination of cash flows from operations and, if necessary, borrowings under its revolving credit facility. The Company’s PUD reserves are supported by a portfolio of development opportunities that are expected to be economic under a wide range of commodity price scenarios. The Company’s development plan is reviewed and approved annually by senior management and the Board of Directors, and is subject to change based on a variety of factors, including commodity prices, service availability and costs, and our assessment of the relative attractiveness of our development opportunities.

As of December 31, 2023, the Company had no PUD reserves that were scheduled to be developed more than five years after initial booking. The Company’s PUD reserves include locations where development has not yet commenced but that are part of our multi-year development plan. The Company’s practice is to book PUD reserves only in locations that are reasonably certain of being drilled within five years from initial booking and where the Company has a final investment decision to proceed with development. The Company’s PUD reserves are based on a development plan that contemplates a steady level of activity across the Company’s core operating areas, with flexibility to adjust as market conditions warrant.

The Company’s PUD reserves are subject to revisions as additional information becomes available from development and appraisal activities, changes in commodity prices and costs, and other factors. Revisions to previous estimates may result from changes in technical estimates, performance of producing wells, additional reservoir information and changes in development plans. The Company’s estimates of PUD reserves are prepared in accordance with SEC rules and are based on internal evaluations by the Company’s reservoir engineers, with oversight and review by our corporate reserves group and independent third-party engineers.

The Company’s ability to develop PUD reserves within the required time period may be affected by a variety of risks and uncertainties, including but not limited to, commodity price volatility, changes in service costs and availability, regulatory changes, access to infrastructure and markets, and operational risks inherent in drilling and completing wells. The Company actively manages these risks through its planning process, hedging program, contracting strategies and operational practices.

The Company’s PUD reserves are an important component of its overall proved reserves and provide visibility into future production and cash flows. The conversion of PUD reserves to proved developed reserves is a key driver of the Company’s operating and financial performance. The Company expects to continue to invest in the development of its PUD reserves in a disciplined manner, with a focus on capital efficiency and returns.

Financial and Operating Overview
Financial and operating results for the three months ended March 31, 2025 compared to the three months ended March 31, 2024 reflect the following:

• Net income increased $164 million from $352 million, or $0.47 per share, in 2024 to $516 million, or $0.68 per share, in 2025.

• Net cash provided by operating activities increased $288 million, from $856 million in 2024 to $1.1 billion in 2025.

• Equivalent production increased 4.8 MMBoe from 62.4 MMBoe, or 693.7 MBoe per day, in 2024 to 67.2 MMBoe, or 746.8 MBoe per day, in 2025.

◦ Oil production increased 3.4 MMBbl from 9.3 MMBbl, or 102.5 MBbl per day, in 2024 to 12.7 MMBbl, or 141.2 MBbl per day, in 2025.

◦ Natural gas production increased 4.5 Bcf from 269.4 Bcf, or 2,993.7 MMcf per day, in 2024 to 273.9 Bcf, or 3,043.8 MMcf per day, in 2025.

◦ NGL volumes increased 0.6 MMBbl from 8.2 MMBbl, or 90.2 MBbl per day, in 2024 to 8.8 MMBbl, or 98.3 MBbl per day, in 2025.

• Average realized prices (including impact of derivatives):

◦ Oil was $69.30 per Bbl in 2025, eight percent lower than the $75.00 per Bbl realized in 2024.

◦ Natural gas was $3.21 per Mcf in 2025, 53 percent higher than the $2.10 per Mcf realized in 2024.

◦ NGLs were $22.28 per Bbl in 2025, 14 percent lower than the $25.82 per Bbl realized in 2024.

• Total pre-tax operating expenses increased $233 million, or $0.86 per Boe, from $3.0 billion, or $47.66 per Boe, in 2024 to $3.2 billion, or $48.52 per Boe, in 2025, due primarily to the following: 

◦ Depreciation, depletion and amortization increased $158 million, or $0.92 per Boe, due to higher production volumes and higher DD&A rates across basins.

◦ Transportation, gathering and processing increased $57 million, or $0.21 per Boe, primarily due to higher Marcellus Shale production volumes.

◦ Taxes other than income increased $45 million, or $0.21 per Boe, due to higher production taxes resulting from higher sales volumes in the Permian Basin and higher commodity prices.

◦ General and administrative expense increased $14 million, or $0.04 per Boe, primarily due to higher compensation-related costs.

◦ Exploration expense increased $12 million, or $0.05 per Boe, primarily due to higher exploratory seismic and geological and geophysical costs in the Permian Basin.

◦ Other operating expenses decreased $53 million, or $0.57 per Boe, primarily due to lower impairments of properties and equipment compared to 2024.

• Income tax expense increased $45 million from $92 million in 2024 to $137 million in 2025, due to higher pre-tax income.

• Capital expenditures increased $145 million from $1.1 billion in 2024 to $1.2 billion in 2025, primarily due to increased development activity in the Permian Basin and Marcellus Shale.

• Free cash flow increased $167 million from $373 million in 2024 to $540 million in 2025, due to higher net income and lower working capital outflows, partially offset by higher capital expenditures.

• The Company returned $248 million to shareholders in the first quarter of 2025 through dividends, consisting of $170 million of base dividends and $78 million of special dividends.

• The Company ended the first quarter of 2025 with $1.9 billion of cash and cash equivalents and $2.2 billion of long-term debt, resulting in net debt of $0.3 billion.

Under the Share Repurchase Authorization, EOG may repurchase shares of its common stock for cash in open market purchases, privately negotiated transactions or otherwise, in accordance with applicable securities laws and other legal requirements. The Share Repurchase Authorization has no time limit, does not require EOG to repurchase any specific number of shares and may be suspended or discontinued at any time.

Our proved reserve estimates as of December 31, 2023 and 2022 were prepared in accordance with SEC rules and definitions. Reserve estimates are inherently uncertain and are based on the evaluation of geological, engineering and economic data. The process of estimating reserves requires the application of judgment and is subject to change as additional information becomes available. Our reserve estimates may change as a result of new information obtained from development and appraisal activities, production history and changes in commodity prices and operating costs.

Our internal reservoir engineering staff prepares our reserve estimates and such estimates are reviewed and approved by our corporate reserves group. The corporate reserves group oversees our reserve estimation process, provides technical support and ensures compliance with our internal controls and procedures related to reserves. Our corporate reserves group is led by our Vice President of Corporate Reserves, who has over 30 years of experience in the energy industry and is a licensed professional engineer. Our reserve estimation process includes internal technical reviews and is subject to oversight by senior management and the Board of Directors.

We also engage independent third-party petroleum engineering firms to audit or prepare estimates of our reserves. For the year ended December 31, 2023, approximately 80 percent of our proved reserves were audited by an independent third-party engineering firm. The independent engineers’ process includes review of property interests, production data, historical price and cost trends, and future development plans provided by us. The independent engineers apply their own judgment and assumptions, and may assign different reserve quantities than our internal staff.

Our reserve estimates are prepared using the average of the first-day-of-the-month prices for the preceding 12-month period (SEC pricing) and include the consideration of future development and production costs, transportation and processing fees, and operating expenses. Prices used for estimating reserves do not include the effects of derivatives. The standardized measure of discounted future net cash flows is calculated using a 10 percent discount rate and SEC pricing, and is intended to provide a common basis for comparing reserve values among companies; however, it should not be viewed as representative of the fair value of our reserves or indicative of the actual results that may be realized.

The estimation of reserves requires the use of significant assumptions, including, but not limited to, estimates of future commodity prices, production decline rates, recovery factors, capital and operating costs, and the timing and amount of future development activity. Changes in these assumptions can have a significant impact on reserve estimates. In addition, regulatory changes and other external factors may impact our ability to develop and produce reserves as planned.

We maintain internal controls over our reserves estimation process, including policies and procedures designed to ensure the completeness, accuracy and consistency of the data used in the estimation process. These controls include segregation of duties, review and approval processes, and documentation of key assumptions and judgments. Our internal audit function periodically reviews our reserves estimation process and reports its findings to senior management and the Audit Committee of the Board of Directors.

Business and Industry Outlook

In 2024, Devon marked its 53rd anniversary in the oil and gas business and its 36th year as a public company. We generated $6.6 billion of operating cash flow in 2024 as a result of the strength of our portfolio of assets and our operational execution. Our portfolio benefited from the acquisition of Grayson Mill that allowed us to efficiently expand our oil production and operating scale while capturing a meaningful runway of highly economic drilling inventory. The transaction created immediate value within our financial framework by delivering sustainable accretion to earnings and free cash flow. Operating cash flow in 2024 remained consistent with 2023, despite a decline in commodity prices, due to operational outperformance, capital efficiency gains and the positive contributions from our Grayson Mill acquisition.

We remain committed to continuing our track record of industry leading return of capital to our shareholders, underpinned by low capital reinvestment rates and a disciplined, returns-driven strategy which is designed to be successful through economic cycles. In 2024, we returned approximately $2.0 billion of cash to shareholders through cash dividends and share repurchases, and will continue to prioritize this shareholder return strategy in 2025.

In 2024, WTI oil prices averaged $75.79 per Bbl versus $77.62 per Bbl in 2023, reflecting a downward trend as oil prices remained volatile even with continued capital discipline by global oil producers. Oil is expected to remain volatile in 2025 due to geopolitical risks to supply, forecasted stronger non-OPEC supply, and improving global demand growth expectations. Henry Hub natural gas prices fell in 2024, averaging $2.27 per Mcf compared to $2.74 per Mcf in 2023. For 2025, natural gas prices are expected to increase compared with 2024 prices due to increased demand, driven by rising LNG exports, strong powerburn as well as discipline from natural gas producers. Our 2025 cash flow is partly protected from commodity price volatility due to our current hedge position that covers approximately 30% of our anticipated oil and gas volumes. In order to further insulate our cash flow, we continue to examine and, when appropriate, execute attractive regional basis swap hedges to protect price realizations across our portfolio.

Our commitment to capital discipline and capital efficiency remains unchanged with our 2025 capital program. Similar to 2024, the majority of our 2025 capital, or approximately 55%, is expected to be focused on our highest returning oil play, the Delaware Basin. Our Williston Basin assets will receive additional capital allocation through 2025 as we work to develop the newly acquired Grayson Mill assets. The remainder of our 2025 capital will continue to be deployed to our other core areas of Eagle Ford, Anadarko Basin and Powder River Basin. Our 2025 capital is expected to be approximately 7% higher than 2024 primarily due to increased activity in the Williston Basin. Due to our strategy of spending within cash flow, we expect to continue generating material amounts of free cash flow for 2025.

Midstream Capacity Constraints and Interruptions Impact Commodity Sales

We rely on midstream facilities and systems owned and operated by others to process our gas production and to gather and transport our oil, gas and NGL production to downstream markets. All or a portion of our production in one or more regions may be interrupted or shut in from time to time due to losing access to plants, pipelines or gathering systems. Such access could be lost due to a number of factors, including, but not limited to, weather conditions and natural disasters, terrorism or sabotage, cybersecurity incidents, accidents, field labor issues or strikes. Additionally, midstream operators have in the past been, and in the future may be, subject to constraints that limit their ability to construct, maintain or repair the facilities needed to gather, process and transport our production. Such interruptions or constraints could adversely impact our operations, including by requiring us to curtail our production or obtain alternative takeaway capacity on less favorable terms.

Our Strategy

Our business strategy is focused on delivering a consistently competitive shareholder return among our peer group. Because the business of exploring for, developing and producing oil and natural gas is capital intensive, delivering sustainable, capital efficient cash flow growth is a key tenet to our success. While our cash flow is highly dependent on volatile and uncertain commodity prices, we pursue our strategy throughout all commodity price cycles with five fundamental principles.

Operating excellence– Operating our business in a safe, reliable and environmentally responsible manner is fundamental to who we are. We embrace innovative thinking and believe technology will be instrumental in the longevity of our industry. With our vision to be a premier independent oil and natural gas exploration and production company, the work our employees do every day contributes to the local, national and global economies. We produce a valuable commodity that is fundamental to society, and we endeavor to do so in a safe, environmentally responsible and ethical way, while striving to deliver strong returns to our shareholders. We have an ongoing commitment to transparency in reporting our ESG performance. We continue to establish new environmental performance targets for our Company and incorporate ESG initiatives into our compensation structure.

Advantaged asset portfolio– We believe U.S. crude oil and natural gas will continue to be advantaged in the global energy markets. As discussed in more detail later in this section, we own a portfolio of assets located in the Delaware Basin, Rockies, Eagle Ford and Anadarko Basin. We strive to own premier assets capable of generating cash flows in excess of our capital and operating requirements, as well as competitive rates of return. We also desire to own a portfolio of assets that can deliver sustainable production extending many years into the future and provide reliable and affordable energy needed to support the world's growing population and energy demands.

Maintaining financial strength and flexibility– Commodity prices are uncertain and volatile, so we strive to maintain a strong balance sheet, as well as adequate liquidity and financial flexibility, in order to operate competitively in all commodity price cycles. Our capital allocation decisions are made with attention to these financial stewardship principles, as well as the priorities of funding our core operations, protecting our investment-grade credit ratings and paying and growing our shareholder dividend. While maintaining financial strength is a top priority, we remain committed to maximizing shareholder value which is evidenced by making opportunistic share repurchases and consistently paying and growing our fixed dividend.

Delivering value to shareholders– We are committed to shareholder returns. We are dedicated to a growing fixed dividend that is sustainable through the commodity price cycles. We adhere to distributing our cash flows in excess of operating and capital needs to shareholders. As we pursue cash flow growth, we continually work to optimize the efficiency of our capital programs and production operations, with an underlying objective of reducing absolute and per unit costs and enhancing our returns.

Cultivating a culture to succeed– We value our people and communities and invest in their success. Our workforce is central to and drives our long-term success. We focus on providing fulfilling careers, meaningful benefits and a sense of inclusion and belonging. We strive to be good stewards in all the communities we operate in, being actively involved and applying our culture of operating excellence.

EOG's website address is www.eogresources.com. Information on our website is not incorporated by reference into, and does not constitute a part of, this report.

At December 31, 2024, EOG's total estimated net proved reserves were 4,748 million barrels of oil equivalent (MMBoe), of which 1,870 million barrels (MMBbl) were crude oil and condensate reserves, 1,358 MMBbl were NGLs reserves and 9,122 billion cubic feet (Bcf), or 1,520 MMBoe, were natural gas reserves (see "Supplemental Information to Consolidated Financial Statements"). At such date, approximately 99% of EOG's net proved reserves, on a crude oil equivalent basis, were located in the United States and 1% in Trinidad. Crude oil equivalent volumes are determined using a ratio of 1.0 barrel of crude oil and condensate or NGLs to 6.0 thousand cubic feet (Mcf) of natural gas.

EOG's operations are all crude oil and natural gas exploration and production related. For information regarding the risks associated with EOG's domestic and foreign operations, see ITEM 1A, Risk Factors.

EOG is focused on being among the highest return and lowest cost producers, committed to strong environmental performance and playing a significant role in the long-term future of energy. EOG operates under a consistent business and operational strategy that focuses on a comprehensive approach to developing acreage through industry cycles. EOG evaluates rate of return, net present value, margins, payback period and other key metrics. This strategy is intended to enhance the generation of cash flow and earnings from each unit of production on a cost-efficient basis, allowing EOG to maximize long-term growth in shareholder value and maintain a strong balance sheet. EOG is also focused on innovation and cost-effective utilization of advanced technology associated with three-dimensional seismic and microseismic data, the development of reservoir simulation models and the use of improved drilling equipment and completion technologies for horizontal drilling and formation evaluation. These advanced technologies are used, as appropriate, throughout EOG to reduce the risks and costs associated with all aspects of oil and gas exploration, development and exploitation. EOG implements its strategy primarily by emphasizing the drilling of internally generated prospects in order to find and develop low-cost reserves. Maintaining the lowest possible operating cost structure, coupled with efficient and safe operations and robust environmental stewardship practices and performance, is integral in the implementation of EOG's strategy.

With respect to information on EOG's working interest in wells or acreage, "net" oil and gas wells or acreage are determined by multiplying "gross" oil and gas wells or acreage by EOG's working interest in the wells or acreage.

Restricted Stock Awards and Units

Restricted stock awards and units are subject to the terms, conditions, restrictions and limitations, if any, that the Compensation Committee deems appropriate, including restrictions on continued employment. Generally, the service requirement for vesting ranges fromonetofour years. Dividends declared during the vesting period with respect to restricted stock awards and units will not be paid until the underlying award vests. Devon estimates the fair values of restricted stock awards and units as the closing price of Devon’s common stock on the grant date of the award, which is expensed over the applicable vesting period.

Performance Share Units

Performance share units are granted to certain members of Devon’s management and employees. Each unit that vests entitles the recipient to one share of Devon common stock. The vesting of these units is based on comparing Devon’s TSR to the TSR of a predetermined group of peer companies and certain indices over the specifiedthree-yearperformance period. Subject to certain limits, the vesting of units may be betweenzeroand200% of the units granted depending on Devon’s TSR as compared to the peer group as of the end of the performance period.

At vesting, recipients receive dividend equivalents with respect to the number of units vested. The fair value of each performance share unit is estimated as of the date of grant using a Monte Carlo simulation with the following assumptions used for all grants made under the plan: (i) a risk-free interest rate based on U.S. Treasury rates as of the grant date; (ii) a volatility assumption based on the historical realized price volatility of Devon and the designated peer group; and (iii) an estimated ranking of Devon among the designated peer group. question: DVN business strategy?
answer: DVNs main goal is to deliver consistently competitive shareholder returns by focusing on sustainable, capital-efficient cash flow growth. This involves operating safely and responsibly, maintaining high-quality assets, keeping a strong financial position, and returning excess cash to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

passages.text:
Our Strategy

Our business strategy is focused on delivering a consistently competitive shareholder return among our peer group. Because the business of exploring for, developing and producing oil and natural gas is capital intensive, delivering sustainable, capital efficient cash flow growth is a key tenet to our success. While our cash flow is highly dependent on volatile and uncertain commodity prices, we pursue our strategy throughout all commodity price cycles with five fundamental principles.

Operating excellence– Operating our business in a safe, reliable and environmentally responsible manner is fundamental to who we are. We embrace innovative thinking and believe technology will be instrumental in the longevity of our industry. With our vision to be a premier independent oil and natural gas exploration and production company, the work our employees do every day contributes to the local, national and global economies. We produce a valuable commodity that is fundamental to society, and we endeavor to do so in a safe, environmentally responsible and ethical way, while striving to deliver strong returns to our shareholders. We have an ongoing commitment to transparency in reporting our ESG performance. We continue to establish new environmental performance targets for our Company and incorporate ESG initiatives into our compensation structure.

Advantaged asset portfolio– We believe U.S. crude oil and natural gas will continue to be advantaged in the global energy markets. As discussed in more detail later in this section, we own a portfolio of assets located in the Delaware Basin, Rockies, Eagle Ford and Anadarko Basin. We strive to own premier assets capable of generating cash flows in excess of our capital and operating requirements, as well as competitive rates of return. We also desire to own a portfolio of assets that can deliver sustainable production extending many years into the future and provide reliable and affordable energy needed to support the world's growing population and energy demands.

Maintaining financial strength and flexibility– Commodity prices are uncertain and volatile, so we strive to maintain a strong balance sheet, as well as adequate liquidity and financial flexibility, in order to operate competitively in all commodity price cycles. Our capital allocation decisions are made with attention to these financial stewardship principles, as well as the priorities of funding our core operations, protecting our investment-grade credit ratings and paying and growing our shareholder dividend. While maintaining financial strength is a top priority, we remain committed to maximizing shareholder value which is evidenced by making opportunistic share repurchases and consistently paying and growing our fixed dividend.

Delivering value to shareholders– We are committed to shareholder returns. We are dedicated to a growing fixed dividend that is sustainable through the commodity price cycles. We adhere to distributing our cash flows in excess of operating and capital needs to shareholders. As we pursue cash flow growth, we continually work to optimize the efficiency of our capital programs and production operations, with an underlying objective of reducing absolute and per unit costs and enhancing our returns.
